findings.title: An implementer-selected remediation base can hide unauthorized intervening paths from both scope checks
findings.reproduction: In `bootstrap_attempt_errors`, a remediation manifest may name any `baseCommit` that is a descendant of the prior candidate (`lineage_base`) and an ancestor of the new candidate. The changedFiles check compares only that selected base to the candidate, and candidate cf8a2568a29766c27a0f73cfb9036d86f91b62ac changes the approved-path scan from `lineage_base..candidate` to the same `evidence_base..candidate` range. Create an unauthorized commit U after the prior candidate P, choose U as the remediation manifest base, then create candidate C containing only an authorized remediation change. Both ancestry checks pass; both diffs inspect only U..C; the unauthorized P..U path is present in C but is omitted from changedFiles and never checked against authorized paths. The added test `test_bootstrap_remediation_scope_starts_at_its_frozen_evidence_base` confirms only that U..C is used and has no adversarial P..U case.
findings.requiredRemediation: Keep manifest changedFiles bound to the exact evidence-base-to-candidate remediation delta, but preserve an authority scan over the complete prior-candidate-to-new-candidate lineage, or equivalently authenticate an exact pre-existing reviewed-state base and separately reject every unauthorized path in the excluded prefix. Add an isolated Git-bound test where an unauthorized path is committed between the prior candidate and claimed remediation base and prove validation rejects it; also retain the current exact remediation chain pass case.
